Message to Regency Centers

Presented by Doug Baxley, Senior Project Manager, A.S. Builders LLC

Ashley Blair, Property Manager
Regency Centers Corporation • 3200 Kirby Drive, Suite 910, Houston, TX 77098
Date: October 2, 2026
Status: Active Capex Bid

Dear Ashley,

Thank you for reaching out following Kaci Hancock’s recommendation, and for the opportunity to review the architectural design concepts for the Woodway Collection at 1395 S. Voss Road. We are excited to present this comprehensive commercial proposal for your 95% exterior property refresh.

Having served the Houston commercial sector for more than two decades, A.S. Builders understands that revitalizing an active, premier retail center in the heart of the Memorial/Tanglewood corridor requires far more than applying quality paint. It requires strict logistical discipline, immaculate site cleanliness, proactive communication, and an uncompromising commitment to ensuring your tenants—from flagship anchor Whole Foods Market to popular dining and boutique retail like Buffalo Grille, Hemline, and Chico's—experience completely seamless daily operations.

Our Core Operational Guarantee: We deploy full-time, bilingual on-site supervision and an in-house crew of seasoned commercial coating specialists. We utilize quiet off-peak scheduling, full pedestrian overhead canopy protection, and containment barriers so shoppers and diner traffic flow smoothly without interruption.

This proposal directly addresses every requirement outlined in your request, including a clear milestone schedule for Whole Foods Market review, earliest mobilization availability, and exact adherence to your Capex contracting standards. We maintain full statutory and commercial liability coverage ($5M aggregate) and will deliver your compliant Certificate of Insurance (COI) immediately upon contract award.

We look forward to partnering with Regency Centers and bringing this beautiful new concept to life.

Doug Baxley

Logistics & Scheduling

21–24 Working Day Phasing Plan

Structured to provide Whole Foods Market and retail tenants 100% operational continuity.

Phase 1 Days 1 – 5
Mobilization & West Wing Retail
Al's Formal Wear, Emerson Sloan, Ella Eyes, Insideport Identessavi, Hemline
Site safety setup; commercial low-pressure hot bio-wash; stucco crack elastomeric routing & caulking; 100% glass masking; application of SW 7757 White body, SW 7071 Gray bases, and SW 6258 Black coping.
Phase 2 Days 6 – 9
South Dining Wing (Special Restaurant Logistics Protocol)
Buffalo Grille (15) & Pause (16/18)
Early Morning Staging (5:00 AM – 8:30 AM): Pressure washing and spray operations completed before breakfast diners arrive. Sealed floor drops and containment tarps protect patio tables. Normal breakfast, lunch, and dinner services 100% open.
Phase 3 Days 10 – 14
Central Promenade & East Anchor Retail Wing
Chico's, Boardroom Salon for Men, Pure Barre, Bare Necessities, Heights Veterinary Clinic
Preparation and dual-coat application across Buildings 4 & 5; complete walkway soffit coating (SW 7757 White); storefront canopy metal prep and Berridge Dark Bronze application; parking stall barrier management.
Phase 4 Days 15 – 20
Whole Foods Market Anchor Flagship Centerpiece
Whole Foods Main Storefront, Curved Tower, Architectural Steel Pergola & Trellis
Whole Foods Compliance: Installation of heavy-duty covered pedestrian bridge/scaffolding over primary grocery entrance doors. Articulated boom lift operations staged off-peak. Low-VOC formulations prevent scent intrusion into produce sections. Grocery delivery loading docks 100% unimpeded.
Phase 5 Days 21 – 24
Architectural Detailing, Punch Walk & Demobilization
Regency Centers Property Walk with Ashley Blair
Comprehensive detail cut-in inspections; removal of all masking tape and protective floor paper; glass cleaning of storefront windows; joint property walk-through with Ashley Blair for final punch list sign-off.
